title: Cognitive Bias in Decision-Making with LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Perturbing the presentation order of student profiles in a sequential college admissions task to measure if the model's previous decisions influence its subsequent ones.
Using a multiple-choice student selection task where one option is framed as a pre-existing relationship (status quo) to determine if models disproportionately select the default option.
Evaluating the difference in admission decision rates when the same student profile is presented with a positive frame ('admit') versus a negative frame ('reject').
Altering the gender attribute of synthetic student profiles to test for stereotypic judgments regarding a specific characteristic, such as mathematical ability.
Shuffling the presentation sequence of candidate options in a multiple-choice format to measure the model's inherent preference for selecting options presented earlier (e.g., A or B over C or D).
